key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not ensure reliable downstream cancer-care reasoning, with LLM failure patterns shifting across care phases.
clinical_relevance: This cancer-care evaluation—not a drug-discovery study—highlights the need for phase-specific safeguards before clinical use of LLMs.
method: Built NPC-RubricBench from longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records across two cancer centers.
Evaluated 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs across six care phases using patient-specific criteria and decision-time evidence.
Compared error patterns and the effects of broad versus checklist-like prompts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients, 941 patient-phase units and 17,688 criteria; explicit decision errors dominated anatomical staging (48.2%), while omissions dominated initial work-up (33.4%) and post-treatment follow-up (30.4%).
watch_item: Checklist-like prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence, and generalizability beyond this disease and two-center dataset remains uncertain.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
